best_for: Windows and Linux users who open odd archive types and want a free, ad-free WinRAR or 7-Zip alternative with strong encryption and a portable build for USB sticks.

points.title: Opens over 200 archive types
points.text: PeaZip extracts 7Z, RAR, ZIP, TAR, ISO, CAB, DMG, ZST and many more. It can create 7Z, ZIP, TAR, ZPAQ, Brotli, Zstandard and its own PEA format, and convert one archive type to another.

points.title: RAR: read yes, write only with WinRAR
points.text: Opening and extracting RAR and RAR5 works out of the box. Creating RAR files needs WinRAR installed on the same machine, because of RAR's licensing.

points.title: Two-factor encryption
points.text: For formats that support encryption you can require both a password and a key file, which makes guessing a weak password far harder.

points.title: Turns clicks into scripts
points.text: Any job set up in the window can be exported as a command-line script from the Console tab. That helps if you want to automate backups or learn the 7-Zip syntax.

points.title: Free and ad-free since 2014
points.text: PeaZip is open source under LGPL 3.0 and free for personal and business use. Windows installers bundled adware from 2011 to 2014; that ended with version 5.3.0, so avoid very old copies from mirrors.

points.title: Portable or installed
points.text: Windows has 32-bit and 64-bit installers for all users plus portable builds that run without installing. The Linux Flatpak covers x64 and Arm64 and is verified by Flathub as published by the developer.

points.title: Mac is separate from this listing
points.text: This site lists Windows and Linux. PeaZip's own site offers Mac builds for Apple Silicon and Intel, and its install steps have you clear a quarantine flag in Terminal before first launch.

points.title: Rolling back
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 43 versions; Linux lists only the current release.
